maps-of-content/audio-engineering-moc.title: Audio Engineering
maps-of-content/audio-engineering-moc.content:
Audio engineering is the practice of recording, processing, and reproducing sound. This area covers the basics of analog and digital audio, dynamics and loudness, stereo and phase, common file formats, and the technical understanding DJs need to make good decisions about sound quality without becoming audio engineers.
Topics

maps-of-content/branding-moc.title: Branding
maps-of-content/branding-moc.content:
Branding is the way people recognize and remember you as a DJ, shaped by your music, professionalism, communication, and consistency. This area covers personal brand and promotional materials, marketing and social media, the business side of booking and pricing, and the long-term career development that builds a lasting legacy.
Topics

maps-of-content/community-moc.title: Community
maps-of-content/community-moc.content:
A community is a group of people connected by a shared interest and mutual contribution, and DJs are part of the community they serve, not separate from it. This area covers culture, inclusivity, and belonging; safety, consent, and respect; and the mentorship, leadership, and reciprocal support that sustain a healthy dance community.
Topics

maps-of-content/creativity-moc.title: Creativity
maps-of-content/creativity-moc.content:
Creativity is the ability to produce original and meaningful musical experiences. This area covers artistic voice and identity, the balance between planning and improvisation, and the ongoing creative process—reflection, evolution, and working through creative blocks—that shapes a DJ’s artistic growth.
Topics

maps-of-content/dj-hardware-moc.title: DJ Hardware
maps-of-content/dj-hardware-moc.content:
DJ hardware is the physical equipment DJs use to control and perform music. This area covers controllers, decks, and mixers; the audio path from interface to PA; performance controls like faders, pads, and jog wheels; and the connections, power, and redundancy that keep a setup reliable.
Topics

maps-of-content/dj-software-moc.title: DJ Software
maps-of-content/dj-software-moc.content:
DJ software is the digital toolset DJs use to organize, prepare, and perform music. This area covers core software concepts—analysis, beat grids, cue points, and playlists—along with library and export workflows, and an overview of the major platforms DJs use today.
Topics

maps-of-content/dj-software-tools-moc.filePath: Maps of Content/DJ Software Tools MOC.md
maps-of-content/dj-software-tools-moc.title: DJ Software Tools
maps-of-content/dj-software-tools-moc.content:
DJ Software tools are the specific programs DJs use to organize, prepare, and perform music.
Topics

maps-of-content/events-moc.title: Events
maps-of-content/events-moc.content:
An event is an organized gathering where DJs create musical experiences for dancers, and different event types have different goals, audiences, and programming needs. This area covers event formats from socials to festivals, time slots and changeovers, and the technical and logistical preparation—riders, venue, sound system—that a performance depends on.
Topics

maps-of-content/foundations-of-djing-moc.filePath: Maps of Content/Foundations of DJing MOC.md
maps-of-content/foundations-of-djing-moc.title: Foundations of DJing
maps-of-content/foundations-of-djing-moc.content:
This area covers the core mindset and philosophy behind DJing: what a DJ actually does, why music matters, how experience design and storytelling shape a set, and the leadership, responsibility, and decision-making skills that separate intentional DJs from those who simply play songs.
Topics

maps-of-content/harmonic-mixing-moc.title: Harmonic Mixing
maps-of-content/harmonic-mixing-moc.content:
Harmonic mixing is the practice of transitioning between songs with compatible musical keys. This area covers musical keys and the Camelot Wheel, harmonic compatibility and clash, tools like key lock and pitch shifting, and why harmonic mixing is one tool among many rather than a rule that overrides musical judgment.
Topics

maps-of-content/health--and--well-being-.title: Health & Well-being
maps-of-content/health--and--well-being-.content:
Health and well-being are essential for long-term success as a DJ, since physical health, mental resilience, and recovery all influence the quality and sustainability of your performances. This area covers physical and mental health, sleep and recovery, hearing and ergonomics, and the stress management and sustainable habits that prevent burnout over a long career.
Topics

maps-of-content/mixing-moc.title: Mixing
maps-of-content/mixing-moc.content:
Mixing is how DJs connect songs together.
This area covers the fundamentals every DJ relies on—beatmatching, phrasing, EQ, and transitions—as well as the advanced techniques, like looping, stems, and effects, that add creativity and control once the fundamentals are solid.
Topics

maps-of-content/music-discovery--and--mu.filePath: Maps of Content/Music Discovery & Music Selection MOC.md
maps-of-content/music-discovery--and--mu.title: Music Discovery & Selection
maps-of-content/music-discovery--and--mu.content:
Music discovery and selection is where DJs learn to build a musical identity, not just collect songs. This area covers finding new music and developing taste, choosing meaningful sources, understanding genre and song function, balancing familiarity with novelty, and curating with intention.
Topics

maps-of-content/music-library--and--orga.filePath: Maps of Content/Music Library & Organization MOC.md
maps-of-content/music-library--and--orga.title: Music Library & Organization
maps-of-content/music-library--and--orga.content:
Music library and organization is where DJs turn a collection of songs into a reliable performance system. This area covers structuring and tagging a library, preparing and quality-checking tracks before a set, backing up your collection, and the ongoing workflows and maintenance that keep everything dependable over time.
Topics

maps-of-content/music-theory-moc.title: Music Theory
maps-of-content/music-theory-moc.content:
Music theory is the study of how music is structured and organized. This area covers the building blocks DJs use to analyze songs and build intentional sets: beat, tempo, and rhythm; how songs are structured into sections like intros, choruses, and drops; and the musical elements—melody, harmony, texture, and dynamics—that shape how a track feels.
Topics

maps-of-content/musical-programming-moc.title: Musical Programming
maps-of-content/musical-programming-moc.content:
Musical programming is the intentional sequencing of songs to create a meaningful experience over time. Mixing is how you connect songs; programming is why you choose them. This area covers song selection and sequencing, energy and set arc, the conversation between songs, and the philosophy that shapes how a DJ builds a journey for the dancefloor.
Topics

maps-of-content/practice-moc.title: Practice
maps-of-content/practice-moc.content:
Practice is the intentional process of improving your DJ skills through repetition, experimentation, and reflection. This area covers deliberate practice and routines, the feedback loop of self-assessment and growth, and the persistence, discipline, and mentorship that sustain long-term development.
Topics

maps-of-content/professionalism-moc.title: Professionalism
maps-of-content/professionalism-moc.content:
Professionalism is consistently acting in a reliable, respectful, and responsible manner. This area covers reliability and preparation, integrity and accountability, and the trust, reputation, and professional relationships that DJs build over the course of a career.
Topics

maps-of-content/reading-the-room-moc.filePath: Maps of Content/Reading the Room MOC.md
maps-of-content/reading-the-room-moc.title: Reading the Room
maps-of-content/reading-the-room-moc.content:
Reading the room is the ability to observe, interpret, and respond to the people on the dancefloor rather than following a predetermined plan. This area covers observation and adaptation, the layers of dancefloor energy and engagement, serving different groups in the room, and how time slots and DJ handoffs shape what a set needs to do.
Topics

maps-of-content/the-loop-academy-moc.content:
This area covers the core mindset and philosophy behind DJing: what a DJ actually does, why music matters, how experience design and storytelling shape a set, and the leadership, responsibility, and decision-making skills that separate intentional DJs from those who simply play songs.

the-loop-academy/01-foundations-of-djing.filePath: The Loop Academy/01 Foundations of DJing/01 Assignment & Reflections.md
the-loop-academy/01-foundations-of-djing.title: Month 1 - Assignment & Reflections
the-loop-academy/01-foundations-of-djing.content:
Put the ideas from Month 1 into practice with your first assignment.

Assignment
Think of someone you know well and create a playlist for that person with a clear intention.
Think about how you want them to feel from beginning to end and what kind of experiences you want them to remember after listening to this playlist.
Submit this in the homework channel as a Spotify playlist for feedback.
Reflection Questions

Who is this playlist for?
What experience are you trying to create?
Why did you choose these songs?
What emotional journey are you creating?
Does the playlist have a turning point, pivot, or defining moment?
Where is the tension?
Where is the release?
What feeling do you want them to remember after listening?
Which songs are the most important in your story, and why?

Next Up
Feedback

the-loop-academy/01-foundations-of-djing.title: Month 1- Feedback
the-loop-academy/01-foundations-of-djing.content:
We’d love to hear your thoughts as you work through the lessons!
Feel free to share your reflections, questions, or insights in our cohort channel. One of the greatest strengths of The Loop is learning from each other’s perspectives.

the-loop-academy/01-foundations-of-djing.title: 01 - Foundations of DJing
the-loop-academy/01-foundations-of-djing.content:
Welcome to the very first month of The Loop Academy.
Before we dive into software, controllers, and mixing, we first want to build something more important:
A way of thinking about DJing.
Great DJs don’t simply play songs. They create experiences.
Throughout the lessons, you’ll hear perspectives from all three founders. Sometimes we’ll agree, sometimes we’ll offer different viewpoints. We believe those conversations are part of becoming a well-rounded DJ.
Topics

Introduction
What is a DJ?
The Purpose of Music
Why DJing Matters in Brazilian Zouk
What Makes a Dancefloor Feel Good
The 5 Layers of DJ Development
Assignment & Reflections
Feedback

Enjoy Month 1, and welcome to the journey. ❤️

the-loop-academy/01-foundations-of-djing.title: Month 1.5 - The 5 Layers of DJ Development
the-loop-academy/01-foundations-of-djing.content:
Technique is the layer most beginner DJs obsess over, but it’s only one piece of five. Playing without any equipment at all - just a phone and an auto-crossfader - can reveal that people, music, and experience are the real foundation, not gear. Different backgrounds and starting points can all converge on the same five layers: Music, Systems, Technique, Musical Direction, and Leadership.



                  
                  Key idea 
                  
                

Technique is only one layer of DJing we can focus on during our growth.


Reflection
Which of the five layers - Music, Systems, Technique, Musical Direction, or Leadership - do you think is currently your strongest? Which is your weakest?
See Also
The Five Layers of DJ Development and Dancefloor Leadership
Next Up
Assignment & Reflections

the-loop-academy/01-foundations-of-djing.filePath: The Loop Academy/01 Foundations of DJing/01 The Purpose of Music.md
the-loop-academy/01-foundations-of-djing.title: Month 1.2 - The Purpose of Music
the-loop-academy/01-foundations-of-djing.content:
Music isn’t just entertainment - it’s the tool a DJ uses to shape emotion, memory, and atmosphere. A single opening track can set an intention for an entire night, using tension, release, and contrast to move a room. Songs also work like chapters in a story, where the meaning of each one depends on what comes before and after it.



                  
                  Key idea 
                  
                

Music is a tool for shaping the experience of the night.


Reflection
Think of a song that changed your mood the moment it started. Was it the song itself, or what it represented for you in that moment?
See Also
The Purpose of Music, Storytelling, and Musical Responsibility
Next Up
Why DJing Matters in Brazilian Zouk

the-loop-academy/01-foundations-of-djing.filePath: The Loop Academy/01 Foundations of DJing/01 What Makes a Dancefloor Feel Good?.md
the-loop-academy/01-foundations-of-djing.title: Month 1.4 - What Makes a Dancefloor Feel Good?
the-loop-academy/01-foundations-of-djing.content:
Dancers won’t follow a DJ into new territory until they trust them first. Starting familiar and slowly building trust can open the door to taking a room somewhere completely different, while pushing too far too fast can empty the floor almost as quickly. Reading the room well means treating a set like a conversation - a constant back and forth between energy, familiarity, and novelty, adjusting based on how dancers respond rather than sticking to a fixed plan.



                  
                  Key idea 
                  
                

Trust is earned before exploration is possible.


Reflection
Do you personally enjoy familiarity or exploration more on the dancefloor, and how might that bias show up in the way you’d DJ?
See Also
Dancefloor Leadership, Leadership vs Control, and Pattern Recognition
Next Up
The 5 Layers of DJ Development

the-loop-academy/01-foundations-of-djing.filePath: The Loop Academy/01 Foundations of DJing/01 What is a DJ?.md
the-loop-academy/01-foundations-of-djing.title: Month 1.1 - What is a DJ?
the-loop-academy/01-foundations-of-djing.content:
A DJ’s job is not to play songs - it’s to create experiences. Beyond simply queuing music, a DJ acts as a music curator, a space facilitator, a storyteller, and a leader, often within the same set. The real craft is finding the right song for the right moment, treating the dancefloor as the true artist while the DJ builds the canvas for it. That responsibility extends beyond any single night - keeping a weekly local social alive requires showing up consistently, long after the initial excitement wears off.



                  
                  Key idea 
                  
                

A DJ’s job is not to play songs. A DJ’s job is to create experiences.


Reflection
Think of a DJ who’s kept a local scene alive for years. What do they actually do, week after week, that a one-off marathon set doesn’t require?
See Also
The DJ’s Role, Experience Design, Musical Responsibility, and Consistency
Next Up
The Purpose of Music

the-loop-academy/01-foundations-of-djing.filePath: The Loop Academy/01 Foundations of DJing/01 Why DJing Matters in Brazilian Zouk.md
the-loop-academy/01-foundations-of-djing.title: Month 1.3 - Why DJing Matters in Brazilian Zouk
the-loop-academy/01-foundations-of-djing.content:
Brazilian Zouk covers an unusually wide musical spectrum - a single night can move from a stripped-back handpan track to heavy drums and vocals within fifteen minutes. That range gives Zouk DJs more creative freedom than DJs in most other partner dance scenes. But more options also mean more responsibility to make every choice feel intentional, whether it’s a 5am closing set or peak time at a huge party.



                  
                  Key idea 
                  
                

Zouk gives DJs extraordinary freedom and extraordinary responsibility in the same time.


Reflection
Think about the most memorable Zouk night you’ve experienced. Was it one specific song, or the range of different experiences across the night?
See Also
Trade-offs and Musical Responsibility
Next Up
What Makes a Dancefloor Feel Good?

the-loop-academy/index.title: The Loop Academy
the-loop-academy/index.content:
The Loop Academy is the 12 month Brazilian Zouk DJ course by the founders of The Loop.
Everything here is built specifically for Brazilian Zouk DJing - written from years of playing in this scene. The curriculum takes you from wherever you are right now - music lover, bedroom DJ, or someone already playing locally - all the way to being ready for international events.
Each month builds on the last. The early months are about listening, musical identity, and building a library you can actually trust. No DJ equipment needed until Month 5.
What you find here: lesson notes, frameworks, homework assignments, and reference material for each month of the course. Use it alongside the videos, or come back to it when you need a reminder of something specific.


                  
                  Note 
                  
                

If you’re on the Resources path, the homework is yours to do at your own pace - no submission needed, just you and the material. If you’re in the Journey, your homework goes to your mentors and peers for feedback each month.
